family.tagline: One partner writes campaigns, one pulls prints, and one Core serves both.
family.story: Zaid is a freelance marketing consultant who works from the sofa end of a converted brick warehouse. Ximena photographs and pulls screen prints at the bench beside the Core. A sleeping platform up a ladder-stair and a walled court out back make up the rest.

home.lede: A converted brick warehouse on a city street, with tall steel-framed windows under a deep parapet. The loft takes the west bay: one tall room, a kitchen along the back wall and a sleeping platform up a ladder-stair. A walled court lies behind.

spots.line: A workbench, a ladder shelf and the Core on the desk.
A mid-century sofa, an ottoman, a hide rug and the bookshelf.
A cooking run along the back wall and a breakfast bar with three stools.
A sleigh bed, a dresser and a record player, up the ladder-stair.

day.line: Ximena draws the next print at the bench.
Zaid writes a client issue from the sofa.
Zaid fills in a content plan at the bar.
The pantry list gets its last item.
Cacao fills in the paper order after lunch.
Zaid takes his reading out to the court.
The open weekend checklist gets its last ticks.
Ximena props the finished set against the brick.

companion.name: Pomelo
companion.job: Drafts client briefs and replies from the context Zaid connected.
companion.limits: Drafts only. Zaid reads and sends every message.

profile.bio: Zaid advises small brands on their campaigns from the sofa end of the loft. His client lists, briefs and posting plans sit on the Core, and Pomelo drafts the replies that he reads before he sends them.

companion.name: Cacao
companion.job: Fills in supplier order forms with the details Ximena typed.
companion.limits: One form at a time. Ximena reads each field and sends it herself.

profile.bio: Ximena photographs for clients and pulls screen prints at the bench beside the Core. Her shoots, line art and press papers sit on the Core, and Cacao fills in the order forms that she checks and sends herself.

popup.title: A parcel at the street door
popup.body: The courier leaves a parcel at the loft's street door. Ximena carries it past the sofa to the desk by the ladder shelf.

popup.title: What is inside the parcel
popup.body: Zaid cuts the tape. Ximena lifts out the Companion Core, a power cable, a quick-start guide and a recovery USB drive.

popup.title: Plugged in on the desk
popup.body: Ximena plugs the cable in beside the monitor. The Core wakes and opens its own Wi-Fi network.

popup.title: Join it from Zaid's phone
popup.body: Zaid joins the Core's own network from his phone, then picks the home network.

popup.title: Zaid and Ximena choose their agents
popup.body: In the Companion Hub store, Zaid picks Hermes and Ximena picks OpenClaw. Companion Memory comes along, with Ghost, Grist, Penpot and PhotoPrism. Then they walk away.

beats.capability: an agent that connects to chat apps, email and more from one self-hosted app

popup.title: Pomelo says hello
popup.body: Zaid messages the agent he named Pomelo from the sofa. The reply comes from the Core, across the loft.
popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

say.speaker: zaid
say.text: Hello, Zaid. I am Pomelo. What should we start with?

detail.before: Without an agent, Zaid wrote every client reply and reminder himself, one app at a time.
detail.after: Pomelo runs in a sandbox on the Core and replies through the messaging app Zaid picked. Those messages travel through that chat service.
steps: Pick Hermes in the Companion Hub store
Give the agent a name
Send it a first message
detail.fact: Hermes runs in its own sandbox on your Core and talks to you through the messaging platform you pick.

beats.capability: draw logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser

popup.title: Three screens from one drawing
popup.body: Ximena draws the line art for a three-colour print in Inkscape on the Core. Each colour gets its own layer, saved beside the shoot.

detail.before: The line art lived in Adobe Illustrator, and every revision became another file on one laptop.
detail.after: Inkscape runs in the browser on the Core, so the drawing and every layer sit in one folder that either of them can open.
steps: Trace the shoot's outline
Give each colour its own layer
Save the file beside the shoot
detail.fact: Inkscape draws logos, diagrams and line art as vector graphics, in your browser.

beats.capability: design and prototype in a web-based design tool you host

popup.title: The open weekend poster
popup.body: Ximena lays out the open-studios poster in Penpot, the photograph and the type side by side. Zaid reads the copy over her shoulder before it goes to print.

detail.before: The poster lived in Figma, and each proof went to the printer as an export from that one file.
detail.after: Penpot holds the layout on the Core, so the type, the photograph and the print file are set in the same place.
steps: Rebuild last year's layout in Penpot
Set the photograph and the type
Export the print file
detail.fact: Penpot is a web-based design tool that you host yourself, for design and prototyping.

beats.capability: edit multi-track video in your browser

popup.title: A reel of the press run
popup.body: Ximena cuts a short reel of the press run in FreeCut, in the browser on her laptop. The clips come from the shoot folder on the Core.
popup.note: FreeCut runs in the browser of the device Ximena edits on.

detail.before: A reel meant a desktop editor and a project folder that lived on one laptop.
detail.after: FreeCut edits multi-track video in the browser of the laptop she works on, with the clips pulled from the shoot folder on the Core.
steps: Pull the press clips from the shoot folder
Cut them to a short reel
Export the reel
detail.fact: FreeCut edits multi-track video in your browser and uses WebGPU on the device you edit on.

beats.capability: an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core

popup.title: Cacao fills in the paper order
popup.body: Cacao opens the paper supplier's website and fills in the sizes Ximena typed. Ximena reads every field, then sends the order herself.
popup.note: OpenClaw reaches websites over your home internet.

say.speaker: ximena
say.text: The form is filled in. Please check the sizes before you send it.

detail.before: Ordering paper meant typing the same sizes and the same address into a supplier's form, field by field.
detail.after: Cacao opens the supplier's page in its browser and fills in the form from what Ximena typed. Ximena reads every field and sends it herself.
steps: Type the sizes and the quantity
Let Cacao fill in the form
Read every field, then send it
detail.fact: OpenClaw is an agent with browser automation and tool use, running in a sandboxed app on your Core.

beats.capability: archive the receipts and contracts you rarely look at

popup.title: The press warranty turns up
popup.body: The press jams after three winters, and the warranty is in Papra on the Core. It was filed with the receipt the week the press arrived.

detail.before: Receipts and warranties went into a Google Drive folder, and finding one meant remembering what it was called.
detail.after: Papra keeps each receipt with its warranty and its date on the Core, so the press's papers come up by name.
steps: Scan the receipt the day it arrives
File it with the warranty
Search for the press's name when it jams
detail.fact: Papra archives the receipts and contracts you rarely look at, until you need them.

beats.capability: track the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place

popup.title: The pantry list by the fridge
popup.body: The loft's shopping list sits in Grocy on the Core, built from what the pantry is running low on. Whoever passes the shop checks it first.

detail.before: The shopping list lived in OurGroceries on two phones, and the pantry lived in nobody in particular.
detail.after: Grocy keeps the pantry stock, the shopping list and the recipes together on the Core.
steps: Count the pantry shelf
Set the level that puts an item on the list
Read the list at the shop
detail.fact: Grocy tracks the pantry, shopping lists, recipes, chores and household habits in one place.

beats.capability: a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file

popup.title: The plan counts its own gaps
popup.body: At the breakfast bar, Zaid keeps a client's content plan in Grist on the Core. A Python formula flags the weeks with nothing booked.

detail.before: A client's plan lived in Airtable, one view for each channel, with the formulas inside that editor.
detail.after: Grist stores the plan as a SQLite file on the Core, with Python formulas, and Zaid can copy the file out with it.
steps: Add a row for each planned post
Write a formula that flags the empty weeks
Copy the file out when a client asks
detail.fact: Grist is a spreadsheet-database with real Python formulas, stored as a SQLite file you can copy.

beats.capability: connect your apps with workflows, with the data staying on your Core

popup.title: The weekly report assembles itself
popup.body: An n8n workflow gathers the week's numbers into a draft report every Thursday morning. Zaid reads the draft before anything goes to the client.

detail.before: The weekly report was stitched together by a chain of Zapier steps, one for each tool.
detail.after: n8n runs the whole workflow on the Core, so the draft is built where the client's numbers already sit.
steps: Pick the week's numbers
Build the draft report
Read it before it goes anywhere
detail.fact: n8n connects your apps with workflows, and the data stays on your Core.

beats.capability: plan and schedule posts across your social accounts

popup.title: Friday's posts wait as drafts
popup.body: Zaid lines up a client's week of posts in Postiz on the Core. Each one stays a draft until he approves it.
popup.note: Posts publish to outside social platforms by design.

detail.before: The week's posts were queued inside Buffer, apart from the briefs they came from.
detail.after: Postiz keeps the queue on the Core, next to the briefs. The posts go out to the platforms only when Zaid approves them.
steps: Write each post from the brief
Set the day for each draft
Approve the week on Friday
detail.fact: Postiz plans and schedules posts across your social accounts.

beats.capability: send invoices and quotes, track expenses and time

popup.title: The gallery's invoice goes out
popup.body: Ximena invoices the gallery for the framed set at the kitchen counter. The quote, the invoice and the expenses sit in Invoice Ninja on the Core.

detail.before: Each invoice was rebuilt from the last one in FreshBooks, and the sale lived in a separate spreadsheet.
detail.after: Invoice Ninja keeps the quote, the invoice and the expenses for each sale together on the Core.
steps: Start from the quote
Add the framing costs
Send the invoice to the gallery
detail.fact: Invoice Ninja sends invoices and quotes and tracks expenses and time.

beats.capability: fill and sign PDF forms on any device, from your own Core

popup.title: The framer signs at the bar
popup.body: The framer from the next bay signs Ximena's commission on a tablet at the breakfast bar. The signed copy lands in a folder on the Core.

Hand over the tablet

beats.capability: keep customers, deals and custom fields in a CRM you host yourself

Paste in the notes from the call
Move the deal along the pipeline

beats.capability: publish a site, a blog or a newsletter you own

popup.title: The client's list comes home
popup.body: A client's newsletter list now sits in Ghost on the Core, beside the drafts. Zaid writes the issue on the sofa and sends it through an outside mailer.

Send it through the connected mailer

popup.title: Pomelo drafts the quarterly brief

popup.note: Messages pass through the chat service you choose.

detail.after: Pomelo drafts the brief on the Core from the thread Zaid connected in Companion Memory. He checks every figure, then sends it himself.

Check each figure against the thread
Send the brief himself

detail.after: BookStack keeps each playbook as a book of chapters and pages on the Core, with search and a history of every edit.

Write the launch notes as chapters
Search for last year's launch

beats.capability: listen to your audiobooks and podcasts, and pick up where you left off on any device

detail.after: Audiobookshelf keeps the audiobooks and the podcasts on the Core and remembers his place on every device.

Group them by room

beats.capability: stream your own music from your Core to a browser or an app

beats.capability: lightweight checklists and notes with Kanban boards and sharing

popup.body: The checklist for the open weekend sits on a Jotty board on the Core. Chairs, posters and sweeping are columns, and both of them move the cards.

detail.before: The weekend jobs lived on a Trello board that only one of them had set up, so the other asked what was left.
detail.after: Jotty keeps the checklist and the board on the Core, shared between both of them.
steps: Make a column for each kind of job
Share the board with both phones
Move a card when the job is done

beats.capability: save web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot

popup.title: The rival's page, saved in time

detail.before: Saved links sat in Raindrop.io, and a page that changed or vanished left only its address behind.
detail.after: Linkwarden saves a screenshot and a PDF of each page on the Core, so the page Zaid read is still the page he reads.
steps: Save the rival's launch page
Let Linkwarden keep a copy
Read the saved copy later
detail.fact: Linkwarden saves web pages with a screenshot and PDF so they survive link rot.

beats.capability: browse and share your photo library, with automatic tagging, without uploading it anywhere

popup.title: Prints against the brick, in daylight
popup.body: Ximena props the finished prints against the court wall by the planter and photographs them in daylight. PhotoPrism sorts the set on the Core by the date it was taken.
popup.note: A photo library is not a backup. Keep the originals.

detail.before: The shoots sat in iCloud Photos, mixed in with everything else on the phone.
detail.after: PhotoPrism browses the shoot library on the Core and tags it automatically, so the finished prints sort by the day they were taken.
steps: Prop the prints against the wall
Add the pictures to the library
Browse the set by date
detail.fact: PhotoPrism browses and shares your photo library, with automatic tagging, without uploading it anywhere.

popup.title: One Core, two kinds of work
popup.body: A press bench, a sofa, a breakfast bar and a court out back, on one Companion Core.

closing.body: Your clients' lists, your drafts and your finished prints can sit on a Companion Core. Browse the Companion Hub store and pick your first apps.

notes: Told in the v3 shape: 19 of 23 room beats are pair beats naming a service from content/story/services.json; the four pair-less ones are Companion Memory, OpenClaw, FreeCut and GlassHome.
Every app is a production-store catalog app with a QA screenshot, so no beat needs an owner entry in reviewed.json. No app here is in more than 14 of the 36 families.
Immich and KitchenOwl are left out on purpose (over, or near, the 40 percent cap): the cast plan now lists PhotoPrism and Grocy for this home in their place.

Honest edges carried: Ghost sends through an outside mailer; Postiz posts to outside platforms and Zaid approves each draft; FreeCut runs in the editing device browser; a photo library is not a backup.
Docuseal makes no claim about signatures. The signer sits at the breakfast bar on the home network: the next bay is a neighbour, not a remote signer.

Camera: no cuts and no tier 2 pose in story:spline. The back court is walked to round the west side of the lot; the platform is one flight up the ladder-stair. One room anchor per room, so no two beats share a shot.
The home has no TV and no desk but the Core desk: the media beat sits at the sofa, and the studio beats stand at the Core desk, the ladder shelf and the room.
Age rule 16: both adults, so Pomelo and Cacao work in their own beats; each agent prepares and Zaid or Ximena approves.
